Are you a small business owner struggling to get found online?
The good news is, you can dominate your local market with targeted keyword research.
It’s about understanding what your ideal customers are searching for when they need your products or services.
At Fused Distribution, we build websites and run SEO specifically for small local businesses
and we’ve found that a solid keyword strategy is the foundation of any successful online presence.
Local keyword research is the process of identifying the specific words and phrases people use when searching for businesses like yours in your area.
Brainstorm Your Services & Products: Make a comprehensive list of everything you offer.
For example, if you’re a landscaping company, think beyond “landscaping” - consider “lawn mowing
Think Like Your Customer: Put yourself in your ideal customer’s shoes.
What problems are they trying to solve?
a potential client looking for a cleaning service might search for “deep cleaning services
Google It - Seriously: Start typing your core services into Google.
Here are a few options: Google Keyword Planner: This free tool (requires a Google Ads account) provides search volume data and keyword suggestions.
You’ll need to estimate your monthly ad spend, but even just using the free version is valuable.
Ubersuggest: Neil Patel’s Ubersuggest offers a limited number of free searches per day and provides keyword ideas
AnswerThePublic: This tool visualizes questions people are asking about your topic
You can use tools like SEMrush or Ahrefs (paid) to get detailed insights into their SEO strategy.
Localize, Localize, Localize: Don’t just add “{Your City}” to your keywords.
If you serve a specific area within your city, include that in your keyword strategy.
see How To Add Photos To Google Business Profile Correctly.
The more specific you are, the better your chances of ranking.
Overlooking Voice Search: People are increasingly using voice assistants like Siri and Alexa to find local businesses.
Optimize your website and content for voice search by using conversational language and answering common questions.
Not Tracking Your Results: Use Google Analytics and Google Search Console to monitor your website’s performance and identify which keywords are driving traffic.
Understanding the balance between keyword volume and keyword difficulty is key to successful local SEO.
Keyword difficulty refers to how competitive a keyword is - how many other websites are already ranking for it.
If you target a keyword with extremely high difficulty, it will be very difficult to rank
